doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Rock and roll, the Beach Boys, Four Freshmen and Motown
summary: He hated AM rock and roll as a teenager, liked the Beach Boys and Four Freshmen harmonies, later enjoyed Motown, and talks of purposeful clams.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did the rock & roll on AM radio enter this picture at all? Was that part of the repertoire?

For me? My sister is a couple of years older than me so I’m the baby in the family. So when rock & roll came out in the ‘60’s when it was happening, and she was driving and I wasn’t driving yet, I was 14 but I mean she was 16. And we’d be driving in the car and she’d have AM radio on and playing all this rock & roll, and I hated it. Oh I hated it. I said, “Turn that off, turn that off, let’s get the FM station so I can hear some jazz in Cleveland.” And I just couldn’t stand it. I really couldn’t. The only group I really enjoyed listening to at all were the Beach Boys ‘cause they had harmonies you know like ‘cause I loved listening to like to well who’s the group, the singing group I love so much — jazz, a wonderful jazz group.

Yeah the Four Freshmen, exactly. The Four Freshmen and that. So for AM records and for pop music the Beach Boys were the closest thing to that as far as ‘cause they had voicings and it was real nice rather than just the rock & roll that was of the day. I did enjoy when Motown came out, this was later though. The Motown came out, and I did a lot of Motown and it was great you know. It was funky and it was loose, it was happy and precision didn’t have to be — it wasn’t part of the picture. You know precision — Buddy’s band — you know he restricted, I mean he was very strict as far as precision but not to a degree of in other words if a clam, a little bubble I’d say, is beautiful you know. I mean a little signature. I do it, sometimes I do it purposely, a little [scats a note] you know a purposeful little thing I did. And then I may introduce that again later on I’ll introduce it to show that it wasn’t a mistake, that it was something that I actually chose to do. It’s, you know it’s — oh gosh, what can I say?
